items.stem: A business buys equipment for cash. How does this affect the accounting equation?

options.text: One asset (equipment) rises and another asset (cash) falls; totals are unchanged
options.rationale: Correct: swapping one asset for another leaves total assets and the equation balanced.
No liability is involved in a cash purchase.

options.text: Equity falls because cash left the business
options.rationale: Paying cash for an asset does not reduce equity; it is an asset swap.
Double-entry keeps the equation in balance after every transaction.

items.explanation: Correct: swapping one asset for another leaves total assets and the equation balanced.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which statements about debits and credits are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A debit increases an asset account
options.rationale: Correct: assets increase on the debit side.

options.text: A credit increases a liability account
options.rationale: Correct: liabilities increase on the credit side.

options.text: Every transaction affects only one account
options.rationale: Double-entry means each transaction touches at least two accounts.

options.text: Debits must always be larger than credits in an entry
options.rationale: Total debits must equal total credits, not exceed them.

items.explanation: Correct: assets increase on the debit side.

items.stem: At period end, a company has earned revenue it has not yet invoiced. Which adjusting entry is needed?

options.text: Accrue the revenue: increase a receivable and recognise the income
options.rationale: Correct: accrual accounting records earned revenue before cash is received.

options.text: Do nothing until the invoice is sent
options.rationale: Accrual accounting recognises revenue when earned, not when invoiced.
A prepayment is cash paid in advance, which is not this situation.

options.text: Reduce equity for the unbilled amount
options.rationale: Earned revenue increases income and equity, it does not reduce equity.

items.explanation: Correct: accrual accounting records earned revenue before cash is received.
